quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Inverted conditional: 'Had' replaces 'If' at the start.
quests.explanation: Had the company invested earlier (inverted third conditional 'if' clause) + it would have avoided the financial crisis (result clause). Inverting 'had' for 'if had' is a formal alternative structure.
quests.textToSpeak: Had the company invested earlier, it would have avoided the financial crisis.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Past perfect 'had already found' shows completion before another past event.
quests.explanation: Subject (the rescue team) + arrived (past) + by the time (time marker) + the hikers had already found shelter (past perfect). 'By the time' shows one action was complete before another began.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers had already found shelter.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Third conditional: hypothetical past result that did not happen.
quests.explanation: If the negotiations had succeeded (third conditional 'if' clause) + thousands of jobs would have been saved (hypothetical result). Third conditionals describe an imagined alternative to what actually happened in the past.
quests.textToSpeak: If the negotiations had succeeded, thousands of jobs would have been saved.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Third conditional with the result clause stated first.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + would have accepted the offer (hypothetical result) + if the salary had matched her expectations (condition). Third conditionals can place the result before or after the 'if' clause.
quests.textToSpeak: She would have accepted the offer if the salary had matched her expectations.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Formal inverted conditional: 'Were... to be' replaces 'If it were'.
quests.explanation: Were the proposal to be approved (formal inverted conditional) + construction would begin almost immediately (result). This formal structure is common in legal and business English.
quests.textToSpeak: Were the proposal to be approved, construction would begin almost immediately.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Past perfect continuous 'had been studying' shows extended prior activity.
quests.explanation: Subject (The scientists) + had been studying the virus (past perfect continuous) + for years (duration) + before the outbreak occurred (time marker). This tense emphasizes the duration of research before the event.
quests.textToSpeak: The scientists had been studying the virus for years before the outbreak occurred.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Formal inverted conditional: 'Should' replaces 'If'.
quests.explanation: Should the situation escalate further (formal inverted conditional) + additional resources will be deployed immediately (result). 'Should' inversion is common in formal warnings and official statements.
quests.textToSpeak: Should the situation escalate further, additional resources will be deployed immediately.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Future perfect 'will have completed' shows completion before a future point.
quests.explanation: By the end of next year (future time marker) + the organization will have completed its restructuring (future perfect). Future perfect describes an action that will be finished before a specified future time.
quests.textToSpeak: By the end of next year, the organization will have completed its restructuring.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Subordinate clause 'Unless' introducing a necessary condition.
quests.explanation: Unless circumstances change dramatically (negative condition) + the trial is expected to begin in March (main clause). 'Unless' sets up an exception to an otherwise expected outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: Unless circumstances change dramatically, the trial is expected to begin in March.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Inverted third conditional with modal 'might have'.
quests.explanation: Had she known about the risks beforehand (inverted third conditional) + she might have made a different choice (hypothetical result). 'Might have' suggests a less certain alternative than 'would have'.
quests.textToSpeak: Had she known about the risks beforehand, she might have made a different choice.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Future perfect 'will have reviewed' marks completion before a deadline.
quests.explanation: Subject (The committee) + will have reviewed all applications (future perfect) + by the time the deadline passes (time marker). This tense emphasizes the review will be finished before that future point.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee will have reviewed all applications by the time the deadline passes.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Subordinate clause 'Provided' introducing a formal condition.
quests.explanation: Provided the funding is approved (formal condition) + the research will proceed as originally planned (main clause). 'Provided that' is interchangeable with 'if', used in formal contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: Provided the funding is approved, the research will proceed as originally planned.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Conditional wish structure 'If only' expressing regret.
quests.explanation: If only the warning had been taken more seriously (regretful wish clause) + the disaster might have been prevented (hypothetical result). 'If only' expresses stronger regret than a simple 'if' clause.
quests.textToSpeak: If only the warning had been taken more seriously, the disaster might have been prevented.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Formal inverted conditional: 'Were it not for' means 'If it weren't for'.
quests.explanation: Were it not for her quick thinking (formal inverted conditional) + the accident could have been far worse (hypothetical result). This structure is a formal way to credit someone for preventing a worse outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: Were it not for her quick thinking, the accident could have been far worse.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Future perfect with 'every component' as the comprehensive object.
quests.explanation: By next month (future time marker) + engineers will have tested every component of the new design (future perfect). 'Every' emphasizes completeness of the testing process.
quests.textToSpeak: By next month, engineers will have tested every component of the new design.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Participial phrase 'Assuming' introduces a condition for the claim.
quests.explanation: Assuming the figures are accurate (condition phrase) + the company's growth has exceeded all expectations (main clause). 'Assuming' is a formal way of saying 'if we accept that'.
quests.textToSpeak: Assuming the figures are accurate, the company's growth has exceeded all expectations.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Inverted third conditional with modal 'could have'.
quests.explanation: Had the team communicated more effectively (inverted third conditional) + the misunderstanding could have been avoided (hypothetical result). 'Could have' emphasizes the possibility that existed.
quests.textToSpeak: Had the team communicated more effectively, the misunderstanding could have been avoided.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Subordinate clause 'As soon as' showing immediate sequence.
quests.explanation: As soon as the results are confirmed (time clause) + the findings will be made public (main clause). 'As soon as' marks an immediate consequence following a condition.
quests.textToSpeak: As soon as the results are confirmed, the findings will be made public.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Inverted clause at the end: 'had... not' replaces 'if... had not'.
quests.explanation: Subject (The negotiations) + would have collapsed entirely (hypothetical result) + had both sides not compromised (inverted condition). The inverted condition can appear after the main clause for formal emphasis.
quests.textToSpeak: The negotiations would have collapsed entirely had both sides not compromised.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Subordinate clause 'Once' showing the result follows completion.
quests.explanation: Once the audit is finalized (time/condition clause) + the board will have a clearer financial picture (result). 'Once' implies the result naturally follows once the condition is met.
quests.textToSpeak: Once the audit is finalized, the board will have a clearer financial picture.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Past perfect continuous 'had been arguing' shows extended prior activity.
quests.explanation: By the time the meeting ended (time marker) + they had been arguing for nearly three hours (past perfect continuous). This tense emphasizes the long duration of the disagreement before the meeting's end.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time the meeting ended, they had been arguing for nearly three hours.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Formal inverted conditional 'Should' for a future possibility.
quests.explanation: Should further evidence emerge (formal inverted conditional) + the case may be reopened for review (result). This formal structure is common in legal language describing future contingencies.
quests.textToSpeak: Should further evidence emerge, the case may be reopened for review.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: First conditional predicting a likely future outcome based on present trend.
quests.explanation: If the climate continues to warm at this rate (condition) + sea levels will rise significantly (predicted result). First conditionals describe realistic future consequences of present conditions.
quests.textToSpeak: If the climate continues to warm at this rate, sea levels will rise significantly.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Inverted third conditional describing a missed opportunity.
quests.explanation: Had the warning system functioned properly (inverted third conditional) + residents would have had more time to evacuate (hypothetical result). This describes how things could have gone differently.
quests.textToSpeak: Had the warning system functioned properly, residents would have had more time to evacuate.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Future perfect 'will have passed away' in contrast with ongoing historical study.
quests.explanation: By the time historians fully understand the event (time marker) + most witnesses will have passed away (future perfect). This contrasts the slow pace of historical understanding with the passage of human life.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time historians fully understand the event, most witnesses will have passed away.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Formal inverted conditional expressing a hypothetical scenario.
quests.explanation: Were the experiment to be repeated (formal inverted conditional) + researchers would likely obtain similar results (hypothetical result). This formal structure is common in scientific and academic writing.
quests.textToSpeak: Were the experiment to be repeated, researchers would likely obtain similar results.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Past perfect 'had already been reviewed' inside a reason phrase.
quests.explanation: Given that the evidence had already been reviewed (reason phrase) + the jury reached its verdict quickly (main clause). 'Given that' introduces a formal reason, similar to 'because'.
quests.textToSpeak: Given that the evidence had already been reviewed, the jury reached its verdict quickly.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: First conditional with a warning about future responsibility.
quests.explanation: If governments fail to act now (condition) + future generations will bear the consequences (predicted result). 'Bear the consequences' is a formal idiom meaning to suffer the results of an action.
quests.textToSpeak: If governments fail to act now, future generations will bear the consequences.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Inverted third conditional describing an alternative timeline.
quests.explanation: Had the funding arrived sooner (inverted third conditional) + the clinic would have opened ahead of schedule (hypothetical result). 'Ahead of schedule' means earlier than originally planned.
quests.textToSpeak: Had the funding arrived sooner, the clinic would have opened ahead of schedule.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Future perfect with 'both companies' as the comprehensive subject.
quests.explanation: By the time the contract expires (time marker) + both companies will have fulfilled their obligations (future perfect). 'Fulfill obligations' means to complete required duties under an agreement.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time the contract expires, both companies will have fulfilled their obligations.
